machine.name: RS Ring Latch Stage A
machine.description: RS bistable forming one half of the minimal provable feedback ring. Reads [S,R] at [16920:16921] and emits [Q,/Q] at [16922:16923]. Paired with RS Ring Latch Stage B to close a two-stage latch ring.

metadata.author: Reality Engine
metadata.description: Two always-active events: SET (10 -> [1,0]) and RESET (01 -> [0,1])

ringCircuit.rationale: Two unique machines, each composed of proven CESs, coupled on coincident lanes. One lap of the ring is exactly two RE -> PE -> RE transitions: each stage's output event is composed into the next universal input event that is presented to the other stage. Because no region remapping is involved, a failure localises to the output-event/merge transition itself rather than to lane translation, which is what makes this the smallest circuit whose connectivity is provable.
provableProperties: two RE -> PE -> RE transitions per lap, one per stage, with no other transfer path available
forward propagation: a SET at stage A reaches stage B only via the universal input event that follows A's output event
feedback propagation: stage B's output event re-drives stage A the same way, closing the ring
state retention: after the external stimulus is withdrawn the ring sustains its state through the merge alone
bistability: the ring latches SET or RESET and holds exactly one of them
quiescence: with both lanes at [0,0] neither stage matches, so the ring rests until driven
testProtocol: reset the universe so no CES progression is carried in
assert both lanes read [0,0] and neither stage emits
drive lane [16920:16921] with [1,0] as an external SET stimulus
step; assert stage A emitted an output event and that it appears in the NEXT universal input event, not the current one
step; assert stage B's initial event consumed lane [16922:16923] and emitted onto lane [16920:16921]
withdraw the external stimulus and step; assert the ring still reads SET (retention through the merge alone)
repeat with [0,1] to prove the RESET state
assert the lap took exactly two output-event/universal-input-event transitions
ringCircuit.transferContract: Nothing passes between machines except through the output event -> universal input event transition. That is the only path. The two stages are addressed on coincident lanes, so the merge needs no region remapping to carry one stage's output into the other's input event — but the transition itself is not skipped and cannot be.
cycleTrace: Stage A initial event matches its input in the current universal input event
Stage A final event emits [Q,/Q] onto lane [16922:16923] as an output event
RE -> PE: the output event is composed into the Output Space Merge
PE -> RE: the next universal input event is presented; Stage B's initial event reads lane [16922:16923]
Stage B final event emits onto lane [16920:16921] as an output event
RE -> PE: second composition into the Output Space Merge
PE -> RE: the following universal input event re-presents lane [16920:16921] to Stage A, closing the lap

governance.notes: Provability fixture for the minimal feedback ring; owned with the digital-logic conformance set.

rules.description: RS Ring Latch Stage A SET to HIGH (1)
RS Ring Latch Stage A RESET to LOW (0)

inputSemantics: RS Ring Latch Stage A set input (S)
RS Ring Latch Stage A reset input (R)
outputSemantics: RS Ring Latch Stage A Q
RS Ring Latch Stage A not-Q

metadata.description: Stage A SET; drives the forward lane [16922:16923] to [1,0]
metadata.actionNarrative: Forward leg asserted: stage B will latch SET on the next cycle.

metadata.description: Stage A RESET; drives the forward lane [16922:16923] to [0,1]
metadata.actionNarrative: Forward leg cleared: stage B will latch RESET on the next cycle.

inputSequences.name: SET Operation

inputSequences.name: RESET Operation
inputSequences.description: Drive the stage from quiescent to reset

inputSequences.name: RING RETENTION
inputSequences.description: Withdraw stimulus; the partner stage re-drives this one
